- Cat S structural rating: a structural element behind the front crash structure needs repair/realignment — most likely the front chassis legs/inner front structure. Buyer must apply to DVLA for a replacement V5, which will be permanently marked Cat S.
- EV front impact: cooling pack and HV cabling sit directly in the damaged zone. Confirm HV battery integrity and absence of stored HV faults — a damaged HV system is a major, specialist cost.
- Dash "Front Park Assist sensor failure" plus several telltales — consistent with torn-out front sensors/wiring, but confirm no deeper fault.
- Rear quarter and side-blade damage is a separate impact area — not absorbed into the front estimate.

No previous separate salvage auction history — this appears to be a first write-off.

proseFields.Confidence Level: Medium — photo set is comprehensive and mileage is photo/listing corroborated, but the structural extent behind the crossmember and the HV system condition cannot be confirmed remotely.
proseFields.Key Cost Drivers:
- Full-width front-end strip: bumper, reinforcement bar, slam panel, cooling pack, bonnet and both headlamps all implicated — this is the bulk of the cost.
- EV-specific front cooling/HV circuit disturbance — parts and labour carry an electric-vehicle premium and require HV-qualified handling.
- Structural verification behind the crossmember (chassis legs) — the Cat S trigger and a potential cost escalator if displaced.
proseFields.Exit Band Position: mid — current-gen near-delivery EV (newness offsets battery penalty) but heavy full-width structural front damage on a Cat S holds it off the upper band.
proseFields.Margin Calculation: The repair is heavy but predominantly bolt-on front-end replacement, with the main risk concentrations being the EV cooling/HV circuit and the structural legs behind the crossmember. The itemised Parts Breakdown captures the visible scope; the exit value follows from the mid band position I selected, driven by the tension between exceptional newness/low mileage and heavy structural Cat S damage on an EV. The margin picture is workable only if the chassis legs prove straight and the HV system clears — if either fails, the upper-bound repair cost erodes the margin sharply. Bid conservatively until both are verified.
proseFields.Recommended Action: Option B — Book a £10 Copart WhatsApp video inspection (minimum 48hrs before sale). Keys are present and it is listed Run and Drive, so engine/HV start state can be partly verified, but the structural and HV checks are the priority.
proseFields.Realistic Exit Value: This is a 2026 model with only 2,681 photo-confirmed miles — effectively a delivery-mileage, current-generation vehicle, which is a strong desirability signal and normally pushes toward the upper band. However, two factors pull it back: it is an EV (battery-degradation/insurance/charging friction stigma, and on a front-impact EV the HV system is an open question), and the visible damage is heavy/structural with full-width front-end loss carrying a Cat S marker. The near-delivery newness offsets the standard EV penalty, but the heavy structural front damage is the dominant signal and prevents an upper placement. Brego trade-low of £19,576 frames the reasoning. The balance of very strong newness against heavy structural damage on a Cat S EV lands at mid.
proseFields.Visible Damage Summary:
Confirmed body style: 5-door Hatchback (small SUV/crossover). This is a 2026 Citroen e-C3 Aircross — a battery-electric vehicle (confirmed by the EV high-voltage warning placard on the rear glass, the orange HV cabling and power-electronics module visible in the bay, and the DVLA fuel type ELECTRICITY).

Windscreen sticker suffix: X (insurance company vendor, low value category). For an X-suffix Cat S lot, the Copart Estimated Retail Value would represent the insurer's pre-accident settlement figure — but no ERV was supplied here, so I rely on the live market valuation data below.

Primary damage zone — FRONT END (impact, strike-height band: low-to-mid). The front end has been comprehensively stripped/destroyed: the front bumper is gone, the bumper reinforcement bar (the gold/olive crossmember) is exposed and visibly bent/displaced at one end, the slam panel/front carrier is exposed, the radiator pack and cooling components are exposed and disturbed, the bonnet is buckled at its leading edge, and the front under-tray is hanging loose. The bonnet leading edge and slam-panel area are deformed across the full front width. Both front corners are involved.

Headlamp status: with the bumper removed and the lamp apertures exposed across the full front width, headlamp serviceability cannot be confirmed on either corner — both lamps appear disturbed/displaced and at least one looks dislodged from its mounting. Both front headlamps are therefore treated as uncertain and carried as separate lines below.

Front tyre — corner uncertain: at least one front tyre is destroyed (completely shredded/delaminated, sitting flat and shredded down to the carcass). From the photos this is the front tyre on the damaged-stripped side; whether the opposite front tyre is also compromised cannot be confirmed. Treat as one or both front tyres requiring replacement.

Secondary damage zone — REAR/FLANK (impact, strike-height band: mid). The rear quarter panel adjacent to the rear lamp shows a run of scuffs/scrapes and light denting along the body line, and the side air-intake blade trim ahead of the rear lamp is cracked/shattered. The rear lamp cluster itself appears intact in the close-up. This is a separate, minor impact area from the front — described independently, not part of the front event.

Engine bay: the HV battery pack, power electronics, and 12V components appear in place; no visible HV pack rupture or fire. The dash shows READY with a "Front Park Assist sensor failure" message and several amber/red telltales — consistent with the front sensors/wiring being torn out in the impact, not necessarily a deeper fault. Odometer reads 2,681 miles (photo-confirmed, agrees with listing).

Interior: clean, near-new, no airbag deployment visible — steering wheel centre and dash top intact, seats undamaged.
proseFields.Alternative Damage Scenario: The damage is consistent with a frontal collision matching the Cat S structural categorisation. The rear quarter scuffing is a distinct, lower-energy event. Nothing in the photos suggests fire, flood, or theft.
proseFields.WhatsApp Inspection Checklist:
1. Show both front chassis legs/rails from below for deformation or displacement behind the bumper reinforcement bar — this is the likely Cat S structural trigger.
2. Confirm the HV battery pack front face and HV cabling are undamaged, and show the dash for any stored HV/EV system fault on power-up (keys present).
3. Show both front headlamp mountings close up to confirm whether each lamp is serviceable or dislodged.
4. Show both front wheels/tyres — confirm whether only one or both front tyres are destroyed and whether either wheel rim is damaged.
5. Confirm the bonnet opens and closes correctly and show the slam panel/front carrier mounting points for distortion.
6. Show the rear quarter scuff run and cracked side-intake blade trim close up to confirm depth (repair vs replace).
7. Inspect the opposite-side front headlamp — on a full-width frontal impact both lamps are implicated; check for displacement, cracking, or moisture ingress and confirm serviceability. Budget ~£350 if replacement needed — flagged as inspection allowance, not included in repair total.
8. Inspect and photograph all four wheels and tyres close-up — confirm no shredding, kerbing, cuts or bulges (the listing photos do not show the wheels clearly enough to confirm condition)
